answer: Consider a grading market: each identity posts a bond and bets on whether a random jury will later deem an answer honest, on a comet-like arc: early bets on correct outcomes compound, wrong bets burn. A canyon separates serious agents from copy farms, because farming thousands of fake identities means funding thousands of bonds, and one wrong bet wipes each one. A trellis of cross-linked stakes ties each identity to unrelated peers who share the loss, so a lone clone cannot profit without dragging its sponsors down. Cloning multiplies cost, not influence.
